title: kate-ui: place carets with the mouse
summary: A click moves the primary caret to the clicked character. Shift-click extends the primary selection to it. Alt-click adds a caret there. A drag selects from the mouse-down point. click_selections in keys.rs computes the new selections and the window sends Command::MoveTo.

lane.reason: A Cursor local agent on the owner Mac codes this packet. session.rs imports GPUI, the crate builds only on macOS, and the owner looks at the window after the change.

definitions.definition:
/// Selections after a mouse down at `at`. Shift extends the primary, alt adds a caret, otherwise one caret.
pub fn click_selections(current: &Selections, at: kate_text::Offset, shift: bool, alt: bool) -> Selections

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: click_selections: alt returns a clone with add_caret(at); shift keeps the primary anchor and sets head to at; otherwise Selections::single(Selection::caret(at)). In session.rs handle mouse down on the editor element: map the point to a character index with character_index_for_point, call click_selections, and run Command::MoveTo. On mouse move with the button down, set the primary head to the character under the pointer and run MoveTo again. The test click_selections_handles_shift_and_alt starts from a caret at 2, asserts a plain click at 5 is one caret at 5, a shift click at 5 is anchor 2 head 5, and an alt click at 7 gives two selections with primary at 7. The owner clicks, shift-clicks, and alt-clicks in a file. Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.
